'''Jangshung''' is an underdocumented [[Sino-Tibetan languages|Sino-Tibetan]] language spoken in [[Kinnaur district]], [[Himachal Pradesh]], [[India]]. Most Jangshung speakers reside in the villages of Jangi, [[Lippa, Kinnaur|Lippa]] and Asrang.<ref>{{citation|last = Negi|first = Harvinder Kumar|year = 2012|title = A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Kinnaura Tribe|journal = Nepalese Linguistics|volume = 27|pages = 101–105|url = https://www.academia.edu/19865965/Sociolinguistic_profile_of_the_Kinnaura_tribe|access-date = 2023-02-01|archive-date = 2023-06-02|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20230602114214/https://www.academia.edu/19865965/Sociolinguistic_profile_of_the_Kinnaura_tribe|url-status = dead}}</ref> They belong to the upper caste, while the lower castes in the same villages speak [[Shumcho language|Shumcho]], a related but distinct language of the Kinnauric branch.<ref  name=oeaw>{{citation|title = Researching and Documenting Endangered Languages of Kinnaur|website = [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]]|url = https://www.oeaw.ac.at/en/phonogrammarchiv/research/endangered-languages-and-dialectology/researching-and-documenting-endangered-languages-of-kinnaur|accessdate = 2023-02-01}}</ref>

Jangshung is closely related to its larger neighbor [[Kinnauri language|Kinnauri]] and sometimes considered one of its [[dialect]]s. Like most language varieties of Himachal Pradesh, Jangshung was occasionally written in the traditional [[Takri script]], but it has largely fallen out of use in the 20th century. Today, it is mostly a spoken language. Most Jangshung speakers are multilingual and typically use [[Hindi language|Hindi]] and [[English language|English]] in writing and other formal contexts.<ref name=oeaw/>
